doc: MiaMe.co.il — the migration phase manifest.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Code deployed to Vercel lands IMMEDIATELY; a migration
lands only when a human runs an approved apply. That asymmetry is the whole
reason a phase model is needed: without one, a reader ships before the column
it reads exists, and the site answers 500 until someone notices.
A PHASE IS ONE APPROVED UNIT OF WORK. One phase per apply run. A phase that
has landed moves to status 'applied' and drops out of the pending menu — a
phase left in the menu after it landed makes the live plan and the approved
plan diverge, and the next run aborts on a plan it cannot reconcile.
THE THREE STATUSES ARE NOT COSMETIC:
applied — present in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations on the MiaMe
project. 'ledger' records the version string production actually
carries, which is NOT always the repo filename prefix.
pending — a real MiaMe migration that has never landed. Eligible to apply.
foreign — written against the SHARED leasing-co-il-prod database, not the
MiaMe data plane. NEVER applied here. See 'why' on each entry.
The 'foreign' status is the finding this file was built to carry. The MiaMe
project holds exactly six tables (events · knowledge · leads · partners ·
vehicle_media_assets · vehicle_media_events). Three files in this directory
address catalog_2026 tables and seo/catalog trigger functions that do not
exist here and never will — they were authored while MiaMe and the leasing
platform shared one database. Applying them against MiaMe does not degrade
anything; it ABORTS, because ALTER FUNCTION on an absent function throws.
Marking them keeps them reviewable without leaving them armed.

phases.title: Pin search_path on seo/catalog trigger fns — SHARED LEASING DATABASE
why: ALTERs public.seo_touch_updated_at() and public.catalog_touch_updated_at().
Measured 2026-08-31 on the MiaMe project: NEITHER function exists, so the
bare ALTER does not degrade — it THROWS, and takes the transaction with it.
Guarded at source on 2026-08-31 so a replay cannot abort on it, but the
status stays foreign: the functions belong to the leasing data plane.

phases.title: SPYQE knowledge rows + MIA FOUR's real supply commitment
why: Two models now, two different waits: MIA FOUR is in stock and ships in up to
3 business days; SPYQE is a pre-order estimated at up to 33. The corpus knew
about neither, so a SPYQE question was answered out of MIA FOUR's rows.
Every embedding is NULL, so retrieval runs entirely on the Hebrew keyword
fallback — and every existing spec-*/price-* row describes MIA FOUR without
saying so. That is why each new row NAMES its model inside the body text and
not only in the id: the keyword path matches the body, so a model name that
lives only in the id is invisible to it.
`spyqe-spec` carries the manufacturer's verified figures; `spyqe-spec-missing`
exists so the assistant has something correct to say about weight, load and
charge time instead of reaching for MIA FOUR's numbers.
It also corrected `lead`, which quoted a balloon payment the simulator does
not offer (Configurator pins balloonPct to 0).
The offer text lives in these rows AND in lib/spyqe.ts. That duplication is
real and deliberate — the corpus is a database, not an import of the bundle —
so when the 248 allocation closes or the price moves, BOTH must be updated.
phases.evidence: applied 2026-08-31 · ledger 20260831210536 · verified live: 36 rows (was 30) · 6 spyqe ids · 0 balloon (was 1) · 0 address · delivery and lead rewritten, their embeddings cleared

phases.title: Drop the ivfflat index that caps retrieval at one document
why: MEASURED on this database 2026-08-31, in a rolled-back transaction: an ivfflat
index built on an EMPTY table with lists=100, then filled with 36 rows, returns
ONE row — for LIMIT 10 and for LIMIT 36 alike. That is the exact shape of
knowledge_embedding_idx, which the schema created before any row existed.
The damage is not the index, it is the interaction. brain/knowledge.ts falls
back to keyword retrieval on ZERO hits (`if (hits.length) return hits`). One is
truthy. So the moment the embedding backfill lands, the brain stops falling back
and starts answering from a SINGLE document instead of four — no error, no log,
no failing check. The awaited backfill would have made retrieval WORSE than the
keyword path it replaced, invisibly. This phase must land BEFORE the backfill.
The fix is no index rather than better parameters: without one, pgvector does an
EXACT cosine scan. Measured, same session, 5,000 rows of 1024-d vectors (139x the
live corpus): Seq Scan + top-N heapsort, 8 of 8 rows, 53.7 ms. At 36 rows it is
sub-millisecond. An ANN index trades accuracy for speed; here there is no speed
to buy and the accuracy is the whole product.
Reversible in full — the rollback recreates the index byte-for-byte, and says in
its own header that doing so reinstates a measured defect.
phases.evidence: applied 2026-08-31 · ledger 20260831212929 · verified live: 0 ivfflat indexes remain (knowledge_body_fts + knowledge_pkey only) · column comment present · 36 rows untouched · security advisor 0 lints · ACCEPTANCE, measured on a faithful 36-row replica running the exact match_knowledge query shape: asked 4 got 4, asked 8 got 8, asked 36 got 36 (before the drop the same test returned 1 for every k)

phases.title: SPYQE answers to its Hebrew name
why: MEASURED 2026-09-01 on the live corpus: 0 rows contain "ספייק", 7 contain
"SPYQE". Retrieval is the Hebrew keyword path (every embedding is NULL) and it
matches on body text — so a buyer typing the natural Hebrew form matched no
SPYQE row and was answered from MIA FOUR rows: the exact cross-model hazard the
SPYQE rows were written to prevent. Raised by the triangle audit (critical),
re-verified independently by SQL before this phase was written.
The fix writes "SPYQE (ספייק)" into the first mention of each of the seven
bodies — full-body rewrites, deterministic and idempotent, with an absolute
postcondition: no row may name SPYQE in Latin only.
The offline fallback in brain/knowledge.ts gets the same treatment in the same
commit, derived from SPYQE.nameHe rather than typed.
phases.evidence: applied 2026-09-01 · ledger 20260901033727 · verified live: 7 rows carry ספייק · 0 rows name SPYQE in Latin only · 36 rows total, untouched count · postcondition enforced in-transaction (raise on any Latin-only row)

phases.title: The catalogue answers to the names the buyer is shown
why: MEASURED on the live corpus 2026-09-01: 3 rows say "4x2", ZERO contain "2×4 City",
ZERO contain "Pro Max", and the pricing category covers 0 SPYQE rows.
lib/models.ts — the source the whole site derives from — names the models
"2×4 City", "2×4 City Long Range" and "4×4 Pro Max". The corpus was using the
internal ids instead. No surface a visitor has seen says "4x2".
Retrieval is the Hebrew keyword path and matches on body text, so a buyer typing
either name the storefront showed them matched NOTHING — and "2x4" matched the
Long Range, answering a question about the entry model with the dearer one.
The fix leads with the real name, keeps the id-style designation as a searchable
alias, carries tagline and price from lib/models.ts, and adds price-spyqe so the
catalogue category covers both products rather than one.
It does NOT move the catalogue into the database: lib/models.ts stays the single
source of truth, and test/catalogAlignment.test.ts fails if the two disagree.
phases.evidence: applied 2026-09-01 · ledger 20260901101217 · verified live: rows naming "2×4 City" 0→2 · "Pro Max" 0→1 · pricing rows 3→4 with 1 SPYQE · corpus 36→37 · three in-transaction postconditions enforced (entry model named, flagship named, pricing covers SPYQE)

phases.title: Financing and ordering answer to the words buyers use
why: MEASURED on the live corpus 2026-09-01: the word "מימון" appeared in EXACTLY ONE
row of 37 — subsidy-disabled, the rehabilitation-branch entitlement for disabled
veterans — and NOT in `finance`, the row that actually describes the payment
terms. Retrieval is the Hebrew keyword path and matches on body text, so
"יש מימון" returned a SINGLE document: a routine commercial question answered out
of a Ministry of Defence benefit, with nothing else in context to correct it.
And no row said how to BUY a MIA FOUR. `lead` described what the simulator sends
without naming the act — no הזמנה, no רכישה, no מזמינים — so "איך אני מזמין" was
answered from the row about paint colour, and once the ranker was fixed, from
SPYQE's pre-order sign-up: the other product, and not a purchase at all.
Both rewrites are minimal and both stay SHORT deliberately. Retrieval normalises
by length, so padding a row with disclosure text pushes it DOWN for the question
it exists to answer — measured: a 290-character `finance` lost "כמה תשלומים אפשר".
The financing disclosure stays where a number is actually quoted (lib/finance.ts
and the simulator); it is not duplicated into a retrieval row.
Ships with the ranker fixes in brain/knowledge.ts in the same commit, because
neither closes the ordering gap alone: the corpus had to name the act, and the
matcher had to stop missing it across Hebrew's final letter forms.
KNOWN LIMIT, recorded rather than papered over: "יש מימון" now ranks `finance`
SECOND, not first. Both rows carry the term once, so length decides, and
subsidy-disabled is shorter. A single-content-word query is settled by length in
this ranker. The embedding backfill is what removes that, not a shorter row.
phases.evidence: applied 2026-09-01 · ledger 20260901121050 · verified live on thhyfwoeybkptxvbpcmg: rows containing מימון 1→2 (finance joins subsidy-disabled) · finance and lead bodies md5-identical to the forward SQL (a1f97f96… / d9e41fe4…) · corpus still 37 rows · both rewritten rows had their embedding cleared (0 embedded, unchanged) · three in-transaction postconditions passed · PRE-FLIGHT: the rollback bodies were md5-checked against the LIVE rows before applying and matched byte-for-byte (b09b3a02… / 1f5538ca…), so the undo is verified rather than asserted · ACCEPTANCE, measured after the fact against the post-apply corpus (md5 98f905ba…, byte-identical to the corpus the before/after was measured on): 25 buyer questions, 4 rank-1 answers corrected and 0 regressions — איך אני מזמין colors→lead · מה הסוללה price-4x2→spec-battery · כמה תשלומים אפשר testride→finance · כמה עולה להשכיר price-4x2→rental; and יש מימון returns 2 documents instead of 1, with finance at rank 2 (subsidy-disabled still ranks first — the known single-content-word limit recorded in `why`, which the embedding backfill removes)

phases.title: Every row names the models as the buyer is shown them
why: MEASURED on the live corpus 2026-09-01, AFTER phase 14 landed: TWO rows still
designate a model by its internal id — `model-choose` and `spec-weight`.
Phase 14 fixed the catalogue and fixed it completely: price-4x2 · price-2x4lr ·
price-4x4 · price-spyqe. Four rows, because four rows were the catalogue. But
naming a model is not the catalogue's privilege — ANY row may do it, and two did.
They sat outside the list the guard checked, so nothing looked at them, and they
kept the exact defect the phase existed to remove.
`model-choose` is the worst place for it to survive: it answers "איך לבחור דגם",
the comparison question a buyer asks BEFORE picking a model — precisely when the
name has to match the storefront. It named all three by internal id, and its
entry-model token was "4×2", which is not even the id (`4x2`): the digits are
reversed relative to the real name, "2×4 City". A designation that exists on no
surface and in no source.
THE ASYMMETRY THAT KEPT IT INVISIBLE: the offline fallback in brain/knowledge.ts
already carried the correct names, and so did lib/seo-pages.ts. Every RENDERED
surface was right; only the live corpus was wrong. So no page ever showed the
defect — it surfaced only when the brain answered a buyer, the one output nobody
reads while developing.
The rewrites add no id-style alias. The aliases belong where someone would type
them — the price rows already carry "הידוע גם כ-4x2" / "…4x4" — and repeating
them would lengthen two short rows for nothing. Retrieval normalises by length,
so padding pushes a row DOWN for the question it exists to answer; measured in
phase 15, not re-learned here.
Ships with the guard that would have caught it: test/catalogAlignment.test.ts
checked four named rows, which is why two unnamed ones sailed through. It now
checks the corpus END STATE for the defect SHAPE, so the next row that names a
model is covered whether or not anyone remembers to list it.
phases.evidence: applied 2026-09-01 15:12:03Z · ledger 20260901151203 · verified live on thhyfwoeybkptxvbpcmg: rows carrying "4×2" 3→0 · rows designating a model by internal id 1→0 · corpus still 37 rows · model-choose and spec-weight bodies md5-IDENTICAL to the forward SQL (718fd8d3… / 5baebff9…) · the two replay-only rows (spec-fold, method-bigfive) matched 0 rows here, exactly as designed — they exist only on a freshly replayed database, which is the environment the correction was written for · three in-transaction postconditions passed · PRE-FLIGHT: the rollback bodies were md5-checked against the LIVE rows BEFORE applying and matched byte-for-byte (4c78bd6a… / 83279c0b…), so the undo is verified rather than asserted · EMBEDDINGS CLOSED IN THE SAME OPERATION: both rewritten rows had their vector cleared (a vector of the old text must not outlive the text), which under the vector-first retriever makes a row reachable only via the keyword top-up — so the backfill was run immediately (knowledge-embed.yml run #2, 15:12:37Z, success) and the result read back from the DB rather than from the workflow's own report: 0 rows awaiting an embedding, 37 distinct vectors. Total window between the rewrite and full re-embedding: ~45 seconds.

phases.title: The corpus can name the entity a buyer is asking about
why: MEASURED on the live corpus 2026-09-01 (37 rows): 0 rows contain "מיה דיינמיקס",
0 contain "MIA FOUR", only 3 contain "קלנועי*" — and NO row answers "what is
מיה פור". That last one is the finding, not the keyword counts.
SPYQE has `spyqe-what`, which states plainly what it is. The MAIN product has no
equivalent: 13 rows mention מיה פור while discussing price, delivery or specs, and
not one says what it IS. An answer engine asked to resolve the entity has nothing
to resolve against, and a buyer asking the same question gets a price quoted at
them instead of an answer.
The vocabulary halves are the same defect the repo already paid for twice: SPYQE
(0 rows contained "ספייק" while 7 contained "SPYQE") and the model names ("4×2",
a designation from no source). Retrieval is keyword-first over body text, so a
term absent from every body is a query that matches nothing — silently, with no
error and no empty state to notice.
TWO rows, because two questions had no answer, not because two keywords were
missing: `mia-four-what` (what it is, under every name it answers to) and
`manufacturer` (who makes it, in both scripts). Both stay SHORT deliberately —
retrieval normalises by length, so padding pushes a row DOWN for the question it
exists to answer; measured in phase 15.
It deliberately does NOT sprinkle the terms through the other rows. A row earns a
word by being about it. A corpus where every row names every term ranks worse:
IDF collapses and length normalisation punishes the padding.
Ships with the on-page half in the same commit — schema alternateName, the
homepage title, and llms.txt — because neither closes the entity gap alone.
phases.evidence: applied 2026-09-02 · ledger 20260902112336 · verified live on thhyfwoeybkptxvbpcmg: corpus 37→39 rows · rows naming the manufacturer in Hebrew 0→2 · rows naming the product in Latin 0→1 · rows saying what it legally is (קלנועי*) 3→4 · three in-transaction postconditions passed · both new rows inserted with a NULL embedding (they have no prior vector to outlive), and the backfill was run immediately rather than left for the next person, since `retrieve` is vector-first and an unembedded row is reachable only through the keyword top-up.
